budget_formulas.negative_inflation_if_positive_exact: D may be replaced by (1+eps)D while P is exact when eps < P/D - 1.
budget_formulas.positive_loss_if_negative_exact: P may be replaced by (1-eps)P while D is exact when eps < 1 - 1/(P/D).
budget_formulas.symmetric_relative_error: P >= (1-eps)P_actual and D <= (1+eps)D_actual imply P>D when eps < (P/D - 1)/(P/D + 1).

candidate.falsifier: If all rows allow large symmetric relative error, then a coarse source-backed inequality might plausibly pay the anti-landing budget.
candidate.mechanism: Treat the exact finite rescue as P>D, where P is positive rescue contribution and D is negative rescue drag.  Compute how much relative error a future source-backed theorem can tolerate while preserving P>D.
candidate.name: coefficient-weighted anti-landing source budget
candidate.prediction: If the route is genuinely near-sharp, the tightest rows will require percent-level or sub-percent control, making broad AP/L1-style estimates inadequate.
candidate.smallest_test: Use the existing anti-landing mass-balance rows and compute one-sided and symmetric relative error budgets.

decision: The coefficient-weighted anti-landing route is near-sharp.  On the post-discovery rows the tightest target is 94856, where P/D is about 1.0191444228.  A symmetric source theorem of the form P >= (1-eps)P_actual and D <= (1+eps)D_actual would need eps below about 0.00948145 on that row.  Therefore broad uniformity, mass-majority, and loose AP-count inputs cannot pay this bridge; a successful proof needs a sharp coefficient-weighted signed binary-prime landing estimate or a different direct witness argument.  Goldbach remains open.
status_boundary: finite source-theorem budget audit only; no anti-landing theorem, signed binary-prime correlation theorem, q286 threshold theorem, strict-central Goldbach theorem, or Goldbach proof
